teach.heading: Where price traveled and where price actually closed are two different pieces of information.
teach.body: A wick shows you that price reached an area. A close shows you that price accepted (or rejected) that area. Those are not the same claim, and mixing them up is one of the most common beginner mistakes on a chart. Price can wick well above a level and still close back below it — that's not the same as price closing above the level. This distinction matters far beyond this lesson: later in the Academy, an entire entry model is built around the rule that a candle has to close past a level, not just poke a wick through it.
teach.dayliNote: "I don't care about the wick. I need the candle to close through the level. Say that back to yourself every time you're tempted to react to a wick." — Dayli Scott

experience.prompt: A candle wicks above a key high but closes back below it. Has that level been broken?

options: no — it wicked through but didn't close through

reinforce.question: Price takes a previous high with a wick but closes back below it. Has bullish structure necessarily been confirmed?
options: No — a wick shows price reached the level, but only a close through it shows acceptance
Yes — any candle touching above the high confirms the break
It depends only on the candle's color, not where it closed

reinforce.question: Tap the candle that closed through the level — not just the one with the longest wick above it.
A wick tells you where price ___. A close tells you where price accepted.
